transcript.content: Hello, welcome. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Hi. Well, I guess what brought me in is that some evenings after work, I've been having this issue with food. Especially on days when I've been really strict with myself all day... I just end up eating way more than I meant to. 

I'll sit down for dinner, but then I'll just keep going. I'll have bowls of cereal, crackers, whatever leftovers are in the fridge, sweets... just eating all of it within a couple of hours.
When you find yourself eating more than you meant to, do you feel like you can't stop or control what you're doing?

Yeah, that's exactly it. Once I get started on those nights, it's like... I just keep going back to the kitchen. Even while I'm in my head telling myself to stop, I just keep eating. I don't really feel back in charge of myself until I'm just completely, uncomfortably full.
After these episodes of eating more than you intend, do you ever try to compensate by making yourself sick, using laxatives, or doing a lot of extra exercise?

No, I don't ever make myself sick or take laxatives. But I do try to make up for it in other ways. 

Usually, the next day after one of those nights, I'll tell myself I need to fix it by just skipping breakfast and lunch entirely. Or... I'll go take an extra-long hike, or push myself a lot harder than usual at my softball conditioning. Even when I'm really tired and don't have the energy, I just feel like I have to do it to work all that food off.

latest_inference.note: This turn ruled out compensatory behaviors such as self-induced vomiting or laxative use, which are features of other eating disorders like bulimia nervosa (F50.2 is consistent as the patient reports recurrent binge eating without regular compensatory behaviors). The patient also reports restrictive behaviors and excessive exercise the day after binges, which aligns with binge eating disorder rather than anorexia nervosa given the absence of sustained restrictive eating patterns.
